item.title: The Catholic Charities Leadership Councils commissioned
item.description: KAPAIA — A commissioning ceremony for Catholic Charities Leadership Councils took place Thursday at Immaculate Conception Church in Kapaia.

item.title: HOOSER: Stepping back from the edge
item.description: Too many issues. Too many challenges. Too many bad and sad things happening in our islands, on the continent, and across the world.

item.title: Happy Camper for Wednesday, January 12, 2026
item.description: Congratulations to Marissa Dennis, the Girl Scouts of Hawaii Kauai island coordinator, for spearheading the free showing of “Gabby’s Dollhouse, The Movie’ (the Girl Scouts even had free patches for the event!) where the Girl Scouts (cookie delivery starts Feb. 19, and volunteers are needed to help unpack the big shipment at the Kauai Veterans Center) were joined by community partners like Hale Opio and the county’s Kauai Emergency Management Agency.

item.title: ‘The Woman In Black’ opens Friday
item.description: PUHI — There will be only three performers, but a lot of special effects when the curtains open Friday on “The Woman in Black,” at the Puhi Theatrical Warehouse, said Liz Hahn of the Kauai Community Players.

item.title: Unbeaten Menehune win Kauai Interscholastic Federation girls basketball Championship
item.description: LIHUE — Waimea High School girls basketball defeated Kapaa, 47-25, on Saturday to emerge as the Kauai Interscholastic Federation Central Pacific Bank champions with a 12-win, 0-loss record in Waimea on the last contest of the KIF girls basketball season.

item.title: Gov. Green blasts federal misinformation as measles cases surge in U.S.
item.description: Gov. Josh Green had strong words regarding the ongoing measles crisis in the U.S., calling it an entirely preventable situation.

item.title: Antisemitism on The Sleeping Giant Trail
item.description: WAILUA — Fourteen examples of antisemitic vandalism were discovered on Sunday at various points along the popular 3.3-mile Nounou Mountain Trail, commonly known as Sleeping Giant Trail.

item.title: Hawaii legislative bill would feed every public school student for free
item.description: Every public school student — regardless of family income — would receive free meals at school under a bill introduced Thursday by nearly half of all 51 House members, including Rep. Scot Matayoshi who saw firsthand what happens to hungry students in class while he taught seventh-­grade science at Nanakuli High &Intermediate School.

item.title: Gov. Green proposes suspension of historic tax breaks in 2027
item.description: Record state tax breaks that went into effect two years ago would be suspended for all Hawaii income earners for three years beginning in the 2027 tax year, Gov. Josh Green said in his State of the State Address Monday.
